You should not use clopidogrel if you are allergic to clopidogrel, or if you have:
any active bleeding; or
a stomach ulcer or bleeding in the brain (such as from a head injury).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
an ulcer in your stomach or intestines; or
a bleeding disorder or blood clotting disorder.
Clopidogrel may not work as well.
This may happen if you have certain genetic factors.
These genetic factors affect the breakdown of this medicine in your body.
Your doctor may perform a blood test to make sure clopidogrel is right for you.
This medicine is not expected to harm an unborn baby.
However, taking clopidogrel within 1 week before childbirth can cause bleeding in the mother.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
You should not breastfeed while using this medicine.

text:

Skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose.
Do not take two doses at one time.

section_heading: What should I avoid while taking clopidogrel?
text:
Avoid alcohol.
Alcohol can increase your risk of stomach bleeding.
Avoid activities that may increase your risk of bleeding or injury.
Use extra care to prevent bleeding while shaving or brushing your teeth.
If you also take aspirin.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist.
Do this before using medicines for pain, fever, swelling, or cold/flu symptoms.
They may contain ingredients similar to aspirin.
These ingredients include salicylates, ibuprofen, ketoprofen, or naproxen.
Taking these products together can increase your risk of bleeding.

section_heading: What other drugs will affect clopidogrel?
text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medications at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you take.
This may increase side effects.
This may make the medications less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a stomach acid reducer such as omeprazole, Nexium, or Prilosec;
an antidepressant such as citalopram, fluoxetine, sertraline, Cymbalta, Effexor, Lexapro, Pristiq, or Prozac;
rifampin;
a blood thinner --warfarin, Coumadin, Jantoven; or
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) --aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may affect clopidogrel.
These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These other drugs also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
